newsitem.title: UK: Alpha Airports sees benefit from US disposal.
newsitem.headline: Alpha Airports sees benefit from US disposal.

text.p: Alpha Airports Group Plc said on Friday its catering services division would receive a "small benefit" during the last quarter of the financial year from the disposal of its U.S. operations.
However, the company said the market in which the division operated would continue to be difficult.
Alpha said its first-half profits were hurt by market pressures on its catering business.
"As a consequence, Alpha Catering Services sustained increased losses in the U.S. and experienced reduced margins in the UK and Amsterdam," the company said in a statement.
The flight services and retail trading group's pretax profits fell 10.7 percent to 10.0 million stg in the first six months ended July 31 against the year-ago period.

First-half operating profits at Alpha's catering services division dropped to 4.3 million stg, down 2.5 million stg from the prior year, with increased losses in the U.S. accounting for the major part of the decline.
As a result of the fall in the company's earnings, Alpha said it kept its interim dividend at 1.75p per ordinary share.
Alpha's shares were down 4.5p at 106 in early trade.
Alpha said it expected to complete the previously-announced 6.8 million stg sale of the loss-making U.S. flight catering kitchens in November.
The disposal excludes a kitchen at Sanford International Airport in Florida.
The company said the disposal would enable it to refocus on its operations in the UK and other parts of Europe.

Among its other businesses, Alpha said its retail services division performed well in the first half, while operating profits from Alpha ground services were in line with expectations at 3.6 million stg.
